summary: Targeted frontend re-test for the two fixed bugs: (1) overlapping TTS audio when clicking speak-btn across verses / rapidly, and (2) speak-btn alignment with share/keep buttons. All scenarios PASS. Instrumented window.Audio via Proxy to count concurrently playing HTMLAudioElement instances and observed max concurrent = 1 across every scenario (verse A -> verse B, rapid same-btn spam, autoplay-while-clicking-another-verse). Waveform appears only for the currently playing verse and disappears on stop/end. Buttons are perfectly aligned (identical bounding-rect top for speak-btn, verse-share-btn, verse-keep-btn on both verses).

alignment.parent_class: mt-4 flex items-center justify-center gap-5 flex-wrap

rapid_same_btn_spam_5x.verdict: no runaway audio; final state settled to stopped as expected by toggle parity

autoplay_then_click_other_verse.verdict: previous audio stopped before new one started

critical_code_review_comments: handleSpeak/stopTts use monotonically increasing ttsSeqRef correctly to invalidate stale in-flight TTS; stopTts pauses ttsRef.current before nulling — good.
Minor: audioCtxRef is reused across plays but ctx.createMediaElementSource is called per play on a fresh Audio element — that is correct (each element only ever gets one source). No leak observed.
Guidance branch wraps SpeakButton in div.mt-4 while non-guidance uses parent flex row (mt-4 flex...); this correctly avoids stray mt-4 misalignment inside the action row.

context_for_next_testing_agent: Overlap detection strategy that works: (a) inject a Proxy on window.Audio pre-navigation to collect all HTMLAudioElement instances into window.__audios, then sample .filter(a=>!a.paused && !a.ended).length on an interval to compute max concurrency; (b) cross-check by counting DOM speak-btn elements whose text is 'silence' (only playing verse) and voice-waveform elements. Both should be <=1 at all times. Intro modal bypass: localStorage.setItem('kali_intro_seen','1') then reload, then click central-golden-dash to open chat.
